title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as new satellite launches and funding initiatives take center stage. Meanwhile, concerns about the health of the ISS and the ongoing challenges in hypersonic testing remind us that not all is smooth sailing in orbit.

themes.title: Satellite Launches Galore
themes.body: Rocket Lab's recent launch of the 10th Synspective satellite underscores the growing trend of commercial satellite deployments. This is complemented by Spain's financial backing of FOSSA's communications push, indicating a robust interest in sovereign satellite capabilities.

themes.title: Defense Budgets on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience highlights a renewed focus on fortifying national security in the orbital arena. With Anduril and L3Harris teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, the defense sector is clearly gearing up for a more competitive space landscape.

themes.title: Concerns Over ISS Health
themes.body: A recent spacewalk to repair the ISS has amplified worries about the station's long-term viability. As the international community grapples with its aging infrastructure, the question of how to sustain human presence in low Earth orbit looms larger.

themes.title: Hypersonic Testing Stumbles
themes.body: The third consecutive delay in hypersonic glide-vehicle testing raises eyebrows about the pace of technological advancement in this critical area. As nations race to develop these capabilities, the setbacks could impact strategic military planning.
